parts.instr: For questions 1–8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).

parts.title: The secret life of octopuses
paras: Octopuses are (0) considered among the most intelligent animals in the sea. In laboratory tests, they have learned to open jars, find their [[1]] through mazes and even recognise individual people.
What makes this so remarkable is that octopuses have a short [[2]] – usually only one or two years – and receive no help from their parents. Everything they know, they must learn [[3]] their own.

Their intelligence is also organised in an unusual way. Around two-thirds of an octopus's nerve cells are [[4]] in its arms rather than its head, which means that each arm can, to some [[5]], act independently.

Octopuses are famous for escaping from aquariums. In one well-known [[6]], an octopus climbed out of its tank at night, crossed the floor and slipped down a pipe that [[7]] to the ocean. Stories like this have [[8]] many scientists rethink what intelligence really means.

q.expl: Устойчивое find your way — найти дорогу. С path, route, road такого выражения нет.
lifespan — продолжительность жизни. Livelihood — средства к существованию, lifestyle — образ жизни, lifeline — спасательный круг.
on their own — самостоятельно. By themselves тоже значит «сами», но by their own — ошибка.
be located — находиться, располагаться. Stationed — о военных, based — о компаниях и людях, settled — поселившийся.
Устойчивое to some extent — до некоторой степени.
in one well-known case — в одном известном случае. Matter и issue — вопрос, проблема; affair — дело, роман.
lead to — вести куда-то (о дороге, трубе). Brought, carried, took требуют дополнения: что именно несли.
После пропуска идёт инфинитив без to (rethink), поэтому подходит только make sb do sth. Cause, lead и force требуют to: caused them to rethink.

parts.name: Open cloze
parts.instr: For questions 9–16, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: Why do we dream?
paras: Everybody dreams, (0) whether or not they remember it in the morning. [[9]] scientists have studied dreams for over a century, they still do not fully agree on why we have them.

One popular theory is that dreaming helps us to deal [[10]] difficult emotions. By replaying stressful events in a safe environment, the brain may be able to reduce the effect they have [[11]] us when we are awake.

Another theory suggests that dreams help us to remember what we have learned. In one study, people [[12]] had played a computer game before going to sleep often dreamed about it, and performed better the next day [[13]] those who had not.

Whatever the reason, most experts agree that it is not worth spending too much time trying to work [[14]] what individual dreams mean. As one researcher put it, 'Your brain is not sending you secret messages. It is simply doing its job, [[15]] is to keep you healthy – [[16]] if it sometimes does so in very strange ways.'

q.expl: Уступка: Although scientists have studied dreams… they still do not agree — хотя… всё же.
deal with sth — справляться с чем-то.
have an effect on sb — влиять на кого-то.
Определительное придаточное к people: people who had played…
Сравнение: performed better … than those who had not.
work out — понять, разгадать.
После запятой which относится к its job: its job, which is to keep you healthy.
even if — даже если.

parts.name: Word formation
parts.instr: For questions 17–24, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals at the end of some of the lines to form a word that fits in the gap in the same line. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: The four-day week
paras: Several companies around the world have been (0) experimenting with a four-day working week. Employees work fewer hours for the same pay, and the early results have been [[17]]. Many firms report that [[18]] has stayed the same or even increased, while staff feel less tired and [[19]]. The number of sick days has also fallen [[20]].

However, the idea is not [[21]] for every type of business. Hospitals and schools, for example, need staff to be [[22]] at all times, and some employees find that squeezing five days of work into four leaves them feeling more [[23]] than before.
Supporters argue that, with careful [[24]], a shorter week could work for most organisations.

q.expl: Результаты обнадёживают — encouraging (описывает результаты). Encouraged описывал бы людей.
После report that нужно подлежащее-существительное: productivity — производительность.
Люди чувствуют себя менее stressed (о человеке). Stressful описывает ситуацию, а не человека.
К глаголу fallen нужно наречие: dramatically — резко.
practical — применимый на практике, удобный.
be available — быть на месте, доступным.
feel pressured / pressurised — чувствовать давление.
После careful нужно существительное: planning. Обрати внимание на удвоение n.

parts.name: Key word transformation
parts.instr: For questions 25–30, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between two and five words, including the word given.
parts.example: 0 What type of music do you like best? FAVOURITE → What IS YOUR FAVOURITE type of music?

q.first: 'Don't touch the paintings,' the guide told us.
q.expl: warn sb not to do sth — предупредить, чтобы не делали. Отрицание ставится перед to.

q.first: It's ages since I last went swimming.
q.expl: It's ages since I last did… ⇄ I haven't done… for ages.

q.first: Perhaps he forgot about the meeting.
q.expl: Предположение о прошлом: may have + V3.

q.first: The film was so good that we watched it twice.
q.expl: so + adj ⇄ such a + adj + noun: It was such a good film that…

q.first: I don't usually go to bed before midnight.
q.expl: be in the habit of doing sth — иметь привычку что-то делать.

q.first: They say the new museum is very impressive.
q.expl: be supposed to be — говорят, что… (считается, что).

parts.name: Multiple choice
parts.instr: You are going to read an extract from a novel. For questions 31–36, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which you think fits best according to the text.
parts.title: Moving to Kerrow
parts.subtitle: In this extract from a novel, fifteen-year-old Nell arrives on a small island with her mother.
paras: The ferry was the only way onto Kerrow, and it ran twice a day when the weather allowed. Nell stood at the rail as the island grew from a grey smudge into something with edges – a harbour, a row of white cottages, a church tower leaning slightly to one side. Her mother had described it as 'peaceful'. Standing there with the wind pulling at her hair, Nell thought 'empty' might have been more accurate.

Their new house was at the top of the hill, a narrow building with a blue door that someone had painted very recently. Inside, it smelled of paint and something older underneath. Her mother moved from room to room, opening windows and making plans out loud. 'Your desk can go here, by the window – look at that view!' Nell looked. The view was mostly sky. She said it was nice, because her mother needed it to be nice, and went upstairs to unpack.

It was the third time they had moved in four years. Each time, her mother had promised it would be the last, and each time Nell had believed her a little less. She had learned not to unpack everything at once. Some boxes stayed taped shut for months, in case they were needed again for the next move. She unpacked her clothes and her books and left the rest by the wall.

That evening she walked down to the harbour on her own. A boy of about her age was sitting on an upturned boat, mending a fishing net with quick, practised movements. He glanced up as she passed and said, without stopping, 'You're the new people in Gull House.' It wasn't a question. Nell had forgotten that on an island everyone would know everything about her before she had even opened her mouth. She felt a familiar urge to turn around and go home, wherever that was.

Instead, for reasons she couldn't have explained, she sat down on the harbour wall. The boy didn't say anything else, and neither did she. The tide came in slowly, lifting the small boats one by one. After a while he held out a section of net and showed her how to tie the knot, and she got it wrong four times before she got it right. When she finally walked back up the hill, it was dark, and she realised she hadn't thought about the next move once.

q.stem: What does the writer suggest about Nell's first view of the island?
opts: She was impressed by how beautiful it was.
She did not share her mother's opinion of it.
She was worried that the ferry would not reach it.
She found it larger than she had imagined.
q.hl: Nell thought 'empty' might have been more accurate.
q.expl: Мама назвала остров «спокойным», а Нелл подумала, что точнее было бы «пустой» — она с мамой не согласна. О красоте и размерах острова она не думает.

q.stem: Why did Nell say the view was nice?
opts: She genuinely liked looking at the sky.
She did not want to disappoint her mother.
She was too tired to argue.
She hoped it would end the conversation quickly.
q.hl: because her mother needed it to be nice
q.expl: Она сказала «мило», потому что маме нужно было это услышать. Сам вид её не впечатлил: «mostly sky».

q.stem: What does the writer suggest by saying that Nell 'had learned not to unpack everything at once'?
opts: She was too disorganised to finish.
She did not expect to stay long.
She did not own many possessions.
She wanted her mother to help her.
q.hl: in case they were needed again for the next move
q.expl: Коробки оставались заклеенными на случай следующего переезда — она не верит, что они останутся надолго.

q.stem: What does 'It wasn't a question' suggest about the boy?
opts: He already knew who Nell was.
He was not interested in her answer.
He had been told to look out for her.
q.hl: on an island everyone would know everything about her
q.expl: Он не спрашивал, а утверждал: на острове все уже знают о новеньких. Недружелюбия в его словах нет (A), и никто не просил его её встречать (D).

q.stem: How did Nell feel when the boy spoke to her?
opts: pleased that he had noticed her
annoyed that he did not stop working
q.hl: She felt a familiar urge to turn around and go home
q.expl: Ей захотелось развернуться и уйти — неприятно, что её уже знают. Ловушка D: он не прервал работу, но раздражения это у неё не вызвало.

q.stem: By the end of the extract, Nell
opts: has decided to stay on the island for good.
has begun to feel more settled.
has become close friends with the boy.
is proud of the skill she has learned.
q.hl: she realised she hadn't thought about the next move once
q.expl: Впервые она ни разу не подумала о следующем переезде — она начинает чувствовать себя здесь своей. Решения остаться навсегда (A) или крепкой дружбы (C) в тексте нет.

parts.name: Gapped text
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a man who learned Japanese in a year. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (37–42). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.
parts.title: One year, one language
parts.subtitle: Software developer Ben Ward decided to learn Japanese from scratch in twelve months. This is how it went.
paras: I had always wanted to learn Japanese, but I kept finding reasons not to start. Then, on my thirtieth birthday, a friend asked me what I would regret never having done. [[37]] The next morning, I downloaded a beginners' course and booked a trip to Tokyo for exactly one year later.

The first month was humbling. Japanese uses three different writing systems, and I struggled to remember even the simplest characters. [[38]] By the end of the second month, though, I could read basic signs and menus.

What made the biggest difference was speaking practice. I found an online exchange partner, Yuki, who wanted to improve her English. [[39]] We spent the first half of each call in English and the second half in Japanese.

I also changed my daily routine. I listened to Japanese podcasts on the way to work and switched my phone's language to Japanese. [[40]] It was frustrating at first, but it forced me to learn words I actually needed.

By month nine, I felt I had hit a wall. I could understand a lot, but whenever I tried to speak quickly, my mind went blank. [[41]] She was right: the problem wasn't my Japanese, it was my fear of making mistakes.

The trip to Tokyo was the real test. I ordered meals, asked for directions and even had a long conversation with a taxi driver about baseball. [[42]] But I came home knowing that a year really can be enough to change your life.

sents.A: Without thinking, I said: learning Japanese.
sents.B: More than once, I seriously considered giving up.
sents.C: We agreed to talk on video twice a week.
sents.D: For a few days, I couldn't even find the alarm settings.
sents.E: Yuki told me I was trying too hard to be perfect.
sents.F: I certainly wasn't fluent, and I made dozens of mistakes.
sents.G: My company even offered to pay for evening classes.

q.expl: Друг спросил, о чём он пожалеет, → «Without thinking, I said: learning Japanese» (A) → на следующее утро скачал курс.
Первый месяц был унизительно трудным → не раз хотел бросить (B) → «By the end of the second month, though…» — контраст.
Нашёл партнёра по обмену → договорились созваниваться по видео дважды в неделю (C) → «We spent the first half of each call…».
Переключил язык телефона на японский → несколько дней не мог найти настройки будильника (D) → «It was frustrating at first…».
В голове пусто, когда говорит быстро → Юки сказала, что он слишком старается быть идеальным (E) → «She was right». Местоимение she отсылает к Юки.
Успехи в Токио → «I certainly wasn't fluent…» (F) → «But I came home knowing…». Ловушка G: про работу в тексте нет ни слова, и «even» не к чему отнести.

parts.name: Multiple matching
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about four unusual museums. For questions 43–52, choose from the museums (A–D). The museums may be chosen more than once.
parts.title: Four museums with a difference

texts.name: The Museum of Lost Things
texts.body: Every object here was once lost by someone – a single glove, a set of keys, a teddy bear left on a train. Each comes with a short note from the person who handed it in, describing where it was found. Some are funny, others surprisingly moving. The museum is tiny – you could see everything in under an hour – but many visitors stay much longer, reading the stories. Entry is free, although donations are welcome. Don't miss the 'reunion wall', which celebrates objects that were eventually returned to their owners.

texts.name: The Sound Museum
texts.body: Rather than looking at objects, visitors here are invited to listen. Headphones are provided at the entrance, and each room recreates the sounds of a different place and time, from a Victorian street market to a 1980s video arcade. Children love the interactive studio, where they can record and mix their own sound effects. The museum gets very busy at weekends, so it's worth booking a time slot online in advance. Allow at least two hours.

texts.name: The Museum of Everyday Design
texts.body: Ever wondered who designed the paperclip, or why a toothbrush looks the way it does? This museum tells the stories behind the ordinary objects we use without thinking. Displays are arranged chronologically, so you can see how a simple item like the kettle has changed over two hundred years. The café on the top floor has excellent views over the river, and the shop sells beautifully designed – if rather expensive – souvenirs. Guided tours run every hour and are included in the ticket price.

texts.name: The Night Museum
texts.body: As its name suggests, this museum only opens after dark. It is dedicated to creatures and activities of the night, from owls and bats to astronomers and night-shift workers. The highlight is the planetarium, where shows run every thirty minutes. Because the building used to be a factory, the rooms are enormous, and some visitors find the lighting a little too dim to read the information panels comfortably. It's a great choice for a rainy evening, but check the website first: it closes completely during the summer months.

q.stem: is not open all year round?
q.hl: it closes completely during the summer months
q.expl: Ночной музей летом полностью закрыт.

q.stem: lets visitors create something of their own?
q.hl: they can record and mix their own sound effects
q.expl: В студии музея звука дети записывают и сводят свои звуковые эффекты.
Вход в музей потерянных вещей бесплатный, только пожертвования. Ловушка C: экскурсия включена в цену билета — значит, билет платный.

q.stem: includes a guided tour in the price of admission?
q.hl: Guided tours run every hour and are included in the ticket price
q.expl: Экскурсии каждый час и входят в цену билета.

q.stem: advises visitors to reserve a visit beforehand?
q.hl: it's worth booking a time slot online in advance
q.expl: В выходные многолюдно, поэтому стоит заранее забронировать время.

q.stem: is in a building that was originally used for something else?
q.hl: the building used to be a factory
q.expl: Здание раньше было фабрикой.

q.stem: displays its objects in the order in which they developed over time?
q.expl: Экспозиция в хронологическом порядке: видно, как менялся чайник за 200 лет.

q.stem: often keeps visitors for longer than its size would suggest?
q.hl: many visitors stay much longer, reading the stories
q.expl: Музей крошечный, но люди задерживаются, читая истории вещей.

q.stem: has a feature that some visitors find inconvenient?
q.hl: some visitors find the lighting a little too dim
q.expl: Некоторым слишком темно, чтобы читать таблички.

q.stem: sells items that are quite costly?
q.expl: Сувениры в магазине красивые, «if rather expensive» — хотя довольно дорогие.
